question: Which of the following gases is evolved when limestone undergoes thermal decomposition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction 'Limestone on heating decomposes into quick lime and carbon dioxide gas' can be represented as,
 
 
• **CaCO₃ (s) heat → CaO (s) +CO₂ (g).**
 
 
 
• 
 
Heat is absorbed in the reaction, so it is an **endothermic reaction.**

 
 
• 
 
This is a decomposition reaction that involves heating, so it is termed as** thermal decomposition**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrogen:**

 
 
• When diluted HCl combines with magnesium, hydrogen is produced.
 
• However, nothing occurs when diluted HCl reacts with mercury or silver because those metals are more reactive than hydrogen and can displace it from HCl.
 
• **2HCl + Mg → MgCl₂ + H₂ **
 
 
 
• **​Oxygen:**
 
 
• **​**The **electrolysis of water** produces oxygen along with hydrogen (H₂). 
 
 
• H₂O → 2H + O
 
 
 
• MnO₂ catalyst is used to heat** potassium chlorate** to produce oxygen, etc.
 
 
• 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂
 
 
 
 
 
• ​​**Carbon monoxide:**
 
 
• When carbon-based fuels like coal, oil, natural gas, and wood are **burned**, carbon monoxide is produced.
 
 
• HCOOH + H₂SO₄ → CO + H2SO4.H₂O
